newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Feb 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Feb 5.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Wednesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* WMX Technologies moved to return its focus to waste management services in a broad corporate makeover that includes more asset sales and 3,000 job cuts.
* U.S. auto sales rose 6.1 percent in January, with Ford Motor sales gaining 2.8 percent and Toyota Motor sales jumping 56 percent.
* Goodyear Tire & Rubber has entered a strategic alliance with Japan's Sumitomo Rubber Industries that should boost Goodyear's international presence.
* Inflation-indexed bonds were sold by the Federal Home Loan Bank System and were a hit with investors.
* Cisco Systems second quarter earnings were slightly above analysts' estimates.
* Apple Computer unveiled a corporate reorganization, but analysts were unimpressed.
* Viacom, which has been unable to sell its 10-station radio group, is now exploring the sale of some individual stations, people familiar with the situation say.
* PepsiCo's fourth quarter earnings plunged 85 percent on charges and poor results in the company's restaurant and international beverage operations.
* A new study shows small companies raised $10.1 billion in venture capital last year with financiers investing in a growing number of entrepreneurial companies.
* The Dow industrials rose 27.32 to 6,833.48, and the dollar strengthened.
* Martha Stewart won control of her business from Time Warner's Time Inc, which will retain a minority interest.
* Italy's Alenia, Sweden's Saab and a South Korean consortium may be participating in Airbus' effort to develop a "superjumbo" passenger jet.
* Sprint's fourth quarter results fell just below Wall Street expectations, but its core long-distance and local-phone businesses posted strong results.
* A successful land auction sent Tokyo stocks up 1.3 percent Tuesday to 18,314.33.
* Canada offered to further loosen its controls on foreign participation in its telecommunications industry.

* Curtain's up on the new year's IPO market. After the customary January lull, the first two big-name initial public offerings of 1997 had their Wall Street premieres yesterday: CarMax Group, a national used car seller, and Vail Resorts, a ski resort operator. -- Heard on the Street.

* Investors who missed out on the Treasury Department's big auction of "inflation-indexed" securities last week suddenly have a group of similar bonds to choose from. Late yesterday the Federal Home Loan Bank System unveiled a $200 million offering of five-year inflation-indexed notes. -- Credit Markets.
